arcane_artifacts.glyph_desc.glyph_arcane: Launches an arcane missile that seeks the nearest hostile creature within 16 blocks, preferring creatures bearing an Arcane Mark, and chases it. It never targets its caster, the caster's team, tamed pets or summons, cannot pass through blocks and gives up a chase after a few seconds. Without a target it flies straight and fades away.

Brands the target with an arcane mark for 8 seconds, visible to every player. A creature can bear only one mark; marking it again refreshes the mark. Arcane Missiles and split projectiles prefer marked creatures.
arcane_artifacts.glyph_desc.glyph_parasi: Binds the struck creature to you with a parasitic link for 8 seconds. While the link holds, every source of damage aimed at you strikes the host instead - before your armor or resistances apply, and with the host's own armor and resistances applied. The link breaks if the host dies or moves more than 32 blocks away. One link at a time; 20 second cooldown. Redirected damage is never redirected again.
arcane_artifacts.glyph_desc.glyph_shrapn: When a projectile augmented with Shrapnel strikes a creature, it splits into two smaller homing projectiles that deal half damage and seek other nearby targets. Split projectiles never split again and do not strike the creature the original projectile hit.
arcane_artifacts.glyph_desc.glyph_pursui: Sharpens the senses of homing projectiles: each Pursuit widens the target search radius, makes the projectile turn more sharply and lets it fly longer. Pursuit never increases damage.
ars_nouveau.augment_desc.glyph_arcane_mi: The missile passes through an additional target or block.
The missile also collides with plants and other non-solid blocks.
Wider search radius, sharper turns and a longer lifetime.
On hitting a creature, splits into two half-damage missiles that seek other targets.
ars_nouveau.augment_desc.glyph_arcane_ma: Increases the duration of the mark.
Decreases the duration of the mark.
ars_nouveau.augment_desc.glyph_projectil: On hitting a creature, splits into two half-damage homing projectiles that seek other targets.
arcane_artifacts.page1.overview: These pages were found tied with a leather cord. Their author never wrote his name - every note is signed only with three question marks. He seems to have been a wizard of the Ars, a restless tinkerer who made each of his artifacts for a very practical need of his own.
arcane_artifacts.page2.overview: His notes describe a Research Table, five worn artifacts and several glyphs. None of them can simply be copied: the wizard insisted that a principle must be understood before it is used, and hid each recipe behind a research. The way to every research is a riddle; the Research Table shows only what you are ready to see.
arcane_artifacts.page3.overview: The artifacts are crafted on the Enchanting Apparatus, the glyphs at the Scribes Table - but only once their research is formulated. Each entry below gives the wizard's own remarks, a description of how the artifact works and its recipe.
arcane_artifacts.page1.rose_gold_ingot: An alloy of copper and gold. Crafting table, shapeless: 4 copper ingots and 4 gold ingots give 2 Rose Gold Ingots. Any copper and gold ingots from the c:ingots tags work. Rose gold stabilises the enchantments of every artifact of this addon and is also used for the Shrapnel glyph.
arcane_artifacts.page1.wreath_of_manipul: Worn on the head. The Wreath studies the damage you suffer and adapts your body to it. It counts separate hits for six damage categories: physical, fire, lava, suffocation, drowning and magic. Falling, starvation, the void and /kill are never counted.
arcane_artifacts.page2.wreath_of_manipul: Adaptation: after 5 hits of one category the Wreath adapts to it for a random 3 to 6 minutes. Physical: Resistance. Fire and lava: Fire Resistance. Suffocation and drowning: Water Breathing. Magic: Arcane Adaptation (magic damage reduced by 25%). Each category has its own counter and timer. While adapted, that counter stays at zero; when the adaptation ends it disappears and you need 5 new hits. Only damage you really took counts: standing in lava counts at the normal hurt rate, damage fully redirected by Parasitism does not count.
arcane_artifacts.page3.wreath_of_manipul: Recovery: if you take no damage for 4 seconds, the Wreath grants Regeneration I for 5 seconds. Any new damage restarts the timer. Cleansing: when a harmful effect that milk could cure (poison, wither, weakness, slowness, hunger...) has stayed on you for 5 seconds without interruption, the Wreath removes it. One effect per cleanse, then a 20 second cooldown.
arcane_artifacts.page4.wreath_of_manipul: Reading the Wreath: its flowers form four groups - silver for physical, orange for fire and lava, turquoise for suffocation and drowning, violet for magic. Grey flowers are dormant, they colour in as hits accumulate and shine brightly while the adaptation is active. Other players see the colours on your head. The tooltip lists every counter and the time left on each adaptation. The adaptation is stored in the Wreath itself and survives death and travel with it.
arcane_artifacts.page1.focusing_boots: Worn in the feet slot. The Boots hold one spell whose form must be Self. Inscribe it like any caster: place the Boots on the Scribes Table and use your spell book on it. A new spell replaces the old one; spells with any other form are refused.
arcane_artifacts.page2.focusing_boots: Starting to crouch casts the inscribed spell on yourself. Holding crouch casts only once; release and crouch again to cast again. The cast goes through the normal spell system: the spell is validated, your mana discounts apply, the mana is paid from your pool, and with too little mana nothing happens and you see the usual message.
arcane_artifacts.page3.focusing_boots: An internal cooldown of 1 second prevents crouch-spamming. Spells cast by the Boots are never repeated by the Focusing Gloves. Good choices: Self + Heal, Self + Leap, Self + Blink, Self + Shield-type effects for an instant defensive reflex.
arcane_artifacts.page1.focusing_gloves: A casting tool, held like a spell book or a wand. Use it to cast the spell inscribed in the gloves: the spell is paid once, then cast a second time a few ticks later for free.
arcane_artifacts.page2.focusing_gloves: Inscribe a spell at the Scribes Table: put the gloves on the table and use a spell book on it. If the spell has no form, the gloves cast it as a Projectile, just like a wand. A spell with its own form keeps it, so Arcane Missile spells work too.
arcane_artifacts.page3.focusing_gloves: The second cast never costs mana and never triggers a third. After a double cast the gloves need 3 seconds to recover. A doubled Parasitism still creates only one link.
arcane_artifacts.page1.ring_of_reversal: Worn as a ring. Each hit you take stores 3 charge in the Ring, up to 100. While worn, every second 10 charge become 2 mana, as long as your mana is not full. The charge is stored on the Ring and shown as a bar on the item.
arcane_artifacts.page2.ring_of_reversal: The Ring can not be farmed: at most one charging hit per second, hits under 1 damage and self-inflicted damage are ignored, and only damage that really reached you counts (armour, invulnerability frames and redirection are applied first). The one-second limit is saved on you, so logging out does not reset it.
arcane_artifacts.page1.mantle_of_reflect: Worn on the back. When a hostile magical projectile is about to hit you, the Mantle has a 15% chance to send it back toward the creature that launched it. After a reflection the Mantle needs 12 seconds to recover.
arcane_artifacts.page2.mantle_of_reflect: Reflected: every Ars Nouveau spell projectile, including Arcane Missiles (they re-target their caster), plus projectiles listed in the arcane_artifacts:reflectable_projectiles tag (blaze and dragon fireballs by default). Never reflected: arrows and other physical projectiles, melee attacks, explosions, projectiles without a living owner, and projectiles from allies. The reflected projectile becomes yours and keeps its spell and speed - it is not amplified.
arcane_artifacts.page1.status_effects: These status effects come from the glyphs and the Wreath. The Parasitism effects only display the state of a link and can not be removed with milk; the link itself decides when they end.
arcane_artifacts.effect_doc.arcane_mark: Placed by the Arcane Mark glyph for 8 seconds. A rune circle turns above the marked creature and every player can see it. A creature carries only one mark; marking it again refreshes it. Arcane Missiles and split projectiles choose marked creatures first. Harmful and curable: milk or Dispel remove it.
arcane_artifacts.effect_doc.parasite_hos: The creature is the host of a parasitic link: all damage aimed at the caster hits it instead, with its own armour and resistances. A tether of particles joins it to the caster. Ends when the link breaks.
arcane_artifacts.effect_doc.parasitic_bo: Shown on the caster while a parasitic link is active. Damage aimed at you is moved to the host before your armour and resistances apply. Void damage and /kill are never moved.
arcane_artifacts.effect_doc.parasitic_re: The Parasitism cooldown: 20 seconds from the moment a link is created. Casting a spell with Parasitism during the cooldown is refused before any mana is spent.
arcane_artifacts.effect_doc.arcane_adapt: Granted by the Wreath of Manipulation when it adapts to magic. Reduces magic damage (magic, wither, dragon breath, sonic boom and Ars Nouveau spell damage) by 25%, after armour.
arcane_artifacts.glyph_doc.glyph_arcane_: How it works: the missile scans 16 blocks around it (more with Pursuit) every few ticks and picks a target in this order: creatures with an Arcane Mark, then monsters and mobs attacking you, then others - the nearest one in each group. It never picks you, your team, your tamed pets or summons, players when PvP is off, or anything behind a wall. It steers toward the target every tick, so it can curve around. If it chases one target for 5 seconds without hitting it, it gives up on that creature for good. Without a target it flies straight; it fades after 10 seconds. On impact it resolves the rest of the spell like a Projectile, and Pierce, Split, Accelerate, Decelerate and Sensitive work as usual. Combos: Arcane Missile - Arcane Mark tags enemies for later missiles; Arcane Missile - Parasitism attaches a link from range; add Shrapnel and Pursuit for a swarm.

How it works: the mark is a status effect, so it is synced to every player and shows as a rotating rune circle. Only one mark exists per creature: a second mark refreshes the duration instead of stacking. Extend Time adds 4 seconds per augment, Duration Down shortens it. The mark itself does no damage - it is a target designator that Arcane Missile and Shrapnel understand.
arcane_artifacts.glyph_doc.glyph_parasit: How it works: when the spell hits a creature, a link is created from you (the caster) to it. For 8 seconds, every time you would be hurt the damage is cancelled at the very first step and dealt to the host instead - before your shield, invulnerability frames, armour, enchantments, Resistance and absorption. The host then applies its own defences. Safety rules: redirected damage is never redirected again (two players linked to each other can not bounce damage); void damage and /kill always reach you; if the host is immune to that damage type (fire on a blaze...), it takes it as parasitic transfer damage instead, so an immune host can not shield you for free. The link breaks when the host dies, goes further than 32 blocks, you die, log out or change dimension. One link at a time and a 20 second cooldown; a second hit (for example the second missile of the Focusing Gloves) neither creates a new link nor extends it.
arcane_artifacts.glyph_doc.glyph_shrapne: How it works: when a projectile carrying Shrapnel hits a creature, two smaller turquoise homing projectiles burst from the impact point. They carry the same spell, deal 50% of its damage and seek the nearest other target - they ignore the creature that was just hit. Split projectiles never split again, so there is no chain reaction, and they cost no mana. Works with Projectile and Arcane Missile; Pursuit on the form also improves the split projectiles. Limit: one Shrapnel per spell.
arcane_artifacts.glyph_doc.glyph_pursuit: How it works: each Pursuit (up to 3) adds 8 blocks to the search radius, makes the projectile turn sharper, lets it chase one target 1 second longer and lets it fly 5 seconds longer. It never changes damage. Pursuit only exists for homing forms such as Arcane Missile, because a straight projectile has nothing to improve.

arcane_artifacts.research.arcane_artifac: Source Resonance
Source gems hum when magic is near. Learn how condensed Source answers to spells.
Cast any spell
Observe an amethyst shard or lapis lazuli to compare
Let a spell effect touch a living creature
Source is not a fuel but a medium: spells travel through it and shape themselves to what they touch.
Trajectories
Arrows fly, eyes of ender seek. Study how a moving spell can be steered.
Cast a Projectile spell
Cast a spell with Accelerate or Decelerate
Strike a creature with Harm or Knockback
A projectile keeps the intent of its caster; given senses, it can follow its target. (Arcane Missile, Pursuit)
Arcane Marking
Glowing ink stays visible in the dark. Can magic leave a sign on a living being?
Cast Sense Magic, or make a creature glow
Hit a creature with Hex or Snare
A spell can leave a trace that other spells recognise. (Arcane Mark)
Fragmentation
Crystals split along their lattice. Could a spell break apart the same way?
Cast a spell with Split
Break or Crush a block with a spell
Magic shatters like crystal: one impact can become several smaller ones. (Shrapnel)
Life Bond
Some creatures feed on others. Study how life force can flow between two bodies.
Wound a creature with Harm
Heal a creature with a spell
Afflict a creature with Wither or Poison
Two lives can be tied so that harm flows from one into the other. (Parasitism)

arcane_artifacts.page1.research_guide: Every research follows three steps. Observation: place a sample in the circle of a Research Table and press Observe. The sample is never consumed. Experiments: the table lists what to try in the world; each experiment is done once and often has several solutions. Formulation: when every experiment succeeded you understand the principle and gain a note; press Formulate to unlock the glyph or artifact.
arcane_artifacts.page2.research_guide: A research you cannot see yet shows as ???. Its page still hints at what is missing: other researches (shown as ??? until you discover them) and glyphs of the Ars that you must already know. Learn the glyph, finish the research - and the page becomes readable.
arcane_artifacts.page3.research_guide: Notes come in four kinds: Material, Biological, Arcane and Spatial. They are not spent: some principles simply require enough experience in a field. Only what you do after a research has begun counts, so start a research before you experiment.
arcane_artifacts.page1.research_table: A table for studying the world. Put a sample in the circle and Observe it: the table names its properties and starts every research the sample belongs to. The right page lists all researches, their experiments and what each one unlocks.
arcane_artifacts.page2.research_table: The table never takes the sample, and everything it confirms is checked by the world itself: experiments are recorded when you really perform them, not when you claim to.
arcane_artifacts.page1.old_parchment: Ordinary paper soaked with Source in an Imbuement Chamber (500 Source, no pedestals), the way an amethyst shard becomes a Source Gem. It ages at once and keeps magical notes without fading.
arcane_artifacts.page1.researcher_notebo: Eight sheets of Old Parchment bound in leather: eight parchments around the edges of a crafting grid, leather in the top right corner. It holds these very notes - the descriptions, the wizard's remarks and every recipe.
arcane_artifacts.lore.research_table: "The Scribes Table copies what is known. I needed a table that would tell me what is not." - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.old_parchment: "My notes kept fading in the damp of the tower. Soaked in Source, paper turns old at once and stays old forever. Old is good. Old does not change." - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.researcher_noteboo: "If you are reading this, I am either dead or very, very late for dinner." - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.rose_gold_ingot: "Copper drinks magic, gold holds it. Melted together they do both - and look rather pretty, which nobody ever believes is the real reason." - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.wreath_of_manipula: "After the third time I set myself on fire in the same week, I decided my body should simply learn. The wreath teaches it." - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.focusing_boots: "Both hands full of reagents, a mimic chewing on my robe - and no way to cast. Now I crouch, and the boots do the rest." - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.focusing_gloves: "Why say a spell twice, when the hands can remember it?" - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.ring_of_reversal: "I am hurt so often that it would be wasteful not to profit from it." - ???
arcane_artifacts.lore.mantle_of_reflecti: "My colleagues from the Archmage council answer arguments with fireballs. The mantle answers them back." - ???
arcane_artifacts.research.arcane_artifac: Flesh Adaptation
Some creatures survive fire, water or blows by changing themselves. Learn how a body adapts to harm.
Get burned
Run out of air underwater or inside a wall
Take a blow from a creature or an arrow
Every harm leaves a lesson the body can learn - and pain itself holds energy. (Wreath of Manipulation, Ring of Reversal)
Focusing
A spell need not live only in a book. Learn how an object can hold a spell and release it.
Cast a spell with Self
Cast a spell with Touch
Cast a spell with Projectile
A spell inscribed into a worn object answers its wearer's movement and repeats itself in skilled hands. (Focusing Boots, Focusing Gloves)
Reflection
Shulkers hide in mirrored shells, shields turn blows aside. Can magic be sent back?
Be hit by a projectile or a spell
Cast Bounce, or knock a creature back with a spell
A moving spell keeps its direction only until something insists otherwise. (Mantle of Reflection)
